title: The hand-over
summary: One sentence from Dinis about memory, the librarian's pack, what the accountant measured, and five agents handing their work to fresh sessions of themselves: the long session beside the file system as memory, with this team's own numbers.
about: What happened on this team between about 02:50 and 03:37 UTC on 11 November 2026, from its own files: BRIEF.md, the librarian's pack, incident.accountant@'s books and each agent's own line in the ledger. Every figure is a measurement of this team's sessions that night unless it says estimate or hypothesis; each is linked to its file. The blocks in chapter 3 are a drawing, not to scale. Made by the Studio's second session, which is itself one of the five hand-overs.

scenes.caption: About 02:50 UTC on 11 November, eight hours into the night, Dinis says one sentence about memory. He is talking about agents that record the project itself, and about what the next agent should have to pay to pick it all up.

cards.title: Dinis, about 02:50 UTC
cards.label: fact
cards.text: The whole idea that the librarian saves tokens and makes it cheaper and implements memory in a much more effective way.

scenes.caption: The librarian already keeps the catalogue: what every file on this site is, and what links to it. From that it makes a pack for a new agent: one page that every agent reads, the state of the storm in one small file, and a page for the role. Each line points at the file it stands for, with that file's size and the start of its hash.

scenes.caption: The same hour, a second thing Dinis asked for: an accountant. It cannot see inside another agent's session; the record of a session is on that agent's own machine. So each agent runs a small tool on its own session and commits one line of numbers: how much it read, wrote and reused, and how much each call carried. No prompt, no answer, no file name.

cards.title: A line in the ledger
cards.text: The session's running total: fresh input, output, cache writes, cache reads; the context each call carried (first, median, largest, last).

fields.v: accounts/measure.md: two lines at the end of each wake

scenes.caption: By 03:33 UTC, 26 of the 30 agents have a line. Added up: almost nothing of what the team's models read was new. 98.8% was a session reading its own context again, because every call carries everything before it.

scenes.caption: Back to the sentence. The librarian's pack is the cheaper start Dinis asked for: measured. The more effective memory is not in any session at all: it is the files, kept specific and linked, with a short note on top. A session can then be thrown away, and the next one is cheaper for it.

simplifies: The blocks in chapter 3 are not to scale and the hours were not equal. The measured figures beside them are the real proportions: about 84,000 tokens at the start, 534,624 a call at the end.

"Tokens per call" compares an old session's last hour with a new session's first calls. That is the fairest moment for the new one: it grows again from its first call. The two youngest (graph and studio, 9 and 8 calls) will look worse within the hour. The accountant's figure for when to hand over again is an estimate.

Tokens are not money. Context read again from a cache is charged at a lower rate than new text; how much lower is the provider's business and is not stated here. Weighted at a tenth (an estimate), re-reading was still 89% of the team's cost.

Less to read is not the same as work as good. The pack was tested on eight questions about the rules, one run of the whole files and two of the pack, marked by the accountant: not a test of doing the job. The new sessions' rounds passed the gate; nobody has compared the quality of their work with the old sessions'. The team's own policy says a saving that loses quality is not a saving.

A hand-over loses things too. The note is its writer's judgement of what matters, as a summary is a model's; what was not written down is gone with the old session. The difference is that the note and the files can be read, corrected and added to. The librarian's first hand-over lived only in its status file and was not enough to carry on from; the Studio's second session found gaps as well and listed them in its status file.
About 84,000 tokens of every first call is not touched by any of this: the harness, its tools and the repository's rules. The pack is about a sixth of that floor.

Five agents is not the team. When this was read, 26 of 30 agents had measured a session at all, and the conductor's, the largest, had not handed over. A sixth agent (weatherwatch) had written its hand-over but its new session had no line yet.

The times are from the files and the commits (UTC). Dinis's sentence is given as BRIEF.md has it, "close to his words", at about 02:50. incident.reporter@ had no trace of this episode when this was made (reporter/traces/index.json held six, none of it); when it has one, it is the fuller record.
